title: Full-Query Security of TWEAKEY Instances
summary: Several TWEAKEY instances are conjectured to achieve full-query security beyond the birthday bound; proving the bound or refuting the conjecture remains open.

formal_statement.body: For the several TWEAKEY instances specified by Jean et al.---ad hoc tweakable blockciphers constructed from key-alternating ciphers with $n$-bit blocks---determine whether they achieve security against up to $2^n$ adversarial queries, surpassing the $2^{n/2}$-query birthday bound. These instances were conjectured to attain full $2^n$-query security but lacked formal security proofs; resolve the conjecture by proving the claimed bound for the specified instances or by refuting it.

scope.domain: Security of TWEAKEY tweakable blockciphers constructed from key-alternating ciphers.
parameters: n: block size in bits, governing the adversarial-query security bounds
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove security against up to 2^n adversarial queries for the specified TWEAKEY instances, or refute the conjecture.

citations.label: How to Build Fully Secure Tweakable Blockciphers from Classical Blockciphers

progress.summary: The paper surveys beyond-birthday-bound constructions and reports that the specified TWEAKEY instances were conjectured fully secure but still lacked formal security proofs. It presents the conjecture as unresolved.
citation_labels: Lei Wang et al., How to Build Fully Secure Tweakable Blockciphers from Classical Blockciphers
